### 2026-10-11 · L0 golden path: `heirloom cve CVE-2026-87975 --line 4.2`

**Done**
- Pushed `stable/4.2.x-heirloom` (= `3396992e83`, tag 4.2.30) and the S2 demo branch `hl/s2-cve-2026-87975` to the fork once the `workflow` scope was granted.
- Built the pipeline in the brief's order:
  - `ledger.py` (SQLite, `(cve, line, stage, attempt)`, an interrupted effect becomes `unknown` and pauses until reconciled);
  - `sources/django_security.py`;
  - `verify/runner.py` (outcome classifier where ERROR never counts as FAIL, plus an in-process `django.__file__` worktree guard);
  - the PRESENCE verdict table with the §9 calibration fixes (staged C4a, added-condition mutant, recursive C4c provenance);
  - LOCATE → PROBE (independent porter with a leakage guard) → CALIBRATE → PRESENCE → ADAPT (headless Claude Code in an Entire worktree) → VERIFY → BEHAVIOUR → DECIDE → PUBLISH (commit, push, artifacts, PR).
- Every stage runs inside a neatlogs child span of a per-CVE WORKFLOW root that carries all §5 attributes; the five detection predicates are mirrored in the ledger.
- Acceptance is scripted in `evals/l0.py` and recorded in [`evals/results_l0.json`](evals/results_l0.json). Every number below comes from that file.

**Results (final code, `c08f4a7`)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 3× from a clean state (`clean --remote` → `cve`) | 3/3 pass: 75.3 s / 77.8 s / 76.7 s; $0.187 / $0.209 / $0.183 per CVE; every stage succeeded first time; PRs #6, #7, #8 (each closed by the next clean) |
| Kill + resume | SIGKILL of the process group while ADAPT's `claude -p` was running (adapt #1 failed, #2 done), then `resume` with injected crashes right after publish.commit, publish.push and publish.pr (each exit 137), then `resume` to completion: exit 0 |
| No duplicates after resume | 1 commit on the fork branch, 1 open PR ([#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/9)), each publish effect done exactly once; all three crashed effects paused as `unknown` and reconciled as "happened" against git/`ls-remote`/`gh` |
| Re-run of a published CVE | no-op in 4.5 s: same commit, same PR, no new stage attempts |
| PR #9 | verdict AFFECTED (C1 C2 C3), `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4MAKVSBHAHH00AQ3PSJM4HN` with the ref on the fork, 12 claims, 0 struck, escalations 0, ledger cost $0.168 (excludes the killed adapt attempt, see below) |
| pytest / ruff / mypy --strict | 83 passed / clean / clean (39 files) |

**Tests that actually ran**
- pytest (83): `test_ledger` (12), `test_django_security` (7, incl. a live check that all 19 post-EOL CVEs have a 5.2 commit and no 4.2 commit), `test_runner` (21, incl. two real runs on the 4.2.30 tree), `test_presence` (13, incl. weakened probe ⇒ UNPROVEN), `test_calibrate` (8, incl. the real `_is_pk_set` refactor trap), `test_probe_rules` (10), `test_claims` (5), `test_detections` (3), `test_decide` (4).
- Inside every pipeline run (Django `runtests.py --parallel=1 -v 2`):
  - the 3 upstream 87975 tests 3× on U⁻ (FAIL) and on U⁺ (PASS);
  - the porter's probe 3× each on U⁻ (FAIL), U⁺ (PASS) and L (FAIL), with coverage on L;
  - the probe 3× on L+fix (PASS);
  - `inline_formsets model_forms model_formsets` (266 tests) on unmodified L and on L+fix: 0 new failures, 0 new skips;
  - the probe + upstream tests on U⁺ and L+fix (BEHAVIOUR: same on all 5 comparable tests).

**Bugs found by the runs (fixed, with tests)**
- The probe validator rejected `from .models import …`, which surfaced as a bogus PROBE_ERROR question ([issue #1](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/1), closed with an explanation).
- Django's `tests/.coveragerc` (`source = django`) overrode `--include`, and coverage keys did not match the mapped paths, so every probe looked like NO_REACH ([issue #2](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/2), closed).
- Artifacts were keyed on the run id, so re-running a published CVE re-published artifacts and edited the PR. They are now keyed on the pushed commit.

**Failures / open problems**
- **neatlogs ingestion:**
  - Of the ~10 pipeline traces, only one has finalized: `d1389e2383`, the 4-second no-op rerun with 14 replay spans and no LLM span. Full runs are `dlq` or `pending` with 0 spans, including PR #9's trace `d67121e6…`, so its span links currently lead to nothing.

- **Lost cost from a killed agent:** a killed `claude -p` attempt's spend is not recorded (the process dies before reporting `total_cost_usd`).
- **Evidence-only publishing missing:** publishing for NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN/UNPROVEN, and `/heirloom answer` polling for open questions, are not built yet (L1).
- **No Entire trailers for this build session:** it started in a repo with no commits (the §9.3 trap), so its commits (`8b3f885`…`c08f4a7`) carry no `Entire-Checkpoint`. Recover with `entire session attach` as was done for B1.

  > **Checkpoint 01M4MAKVSBHAHH00AQ3PSJM4HN** · session `030f083b-38a0-4506-8ce7-1c8b0032bb7f` · 2026-10-11 01:53:08 · 199.2k tokens · commit `8e263e5` [4.2.x] Fixed CVE-2026-87975 -- Prevented forging actions in model formsets with editable PKs.
  >
  > **Intent:** Backport security fix for CVE-2026-87975 from Django 5.2 to Django 4.2, preventing forged POST data from deleting or creating objects outside a ModelFormSet's queryset via editable primary keys.
  >
  > **Outcome:** Successfully applied a one-line fix to `django/forms/models.py` adding `or obj._state.adding` to the existing `obj.pk is None` guard in `save_existing_objects()`. All 3 CVE probe tests and all 74 `model_formsets` regression tests pass.
  >
  > **Learnings (repository):** Django 4.2 uses `obj.pk is None` directly rather than the `obj._is_pk_set()` helper introduced in 5.x, so backports must preserve the older idiom. Django sets `_state.adding = False` only after a successful database fetch; instances constructed in memory (via `construct_instance()` or `BaseInlineFormSet` parent-link assignment) retain `_state.adding = True` even if their PK field is later populated.
  >
  > **Learnings (code):** `django/forms/models.py:909-933`: `BaseModelFormSet.save_existing_objects()` iterated `initial_forms` and used `obj.pk is None` as the sole guard against acting on instances not fetched from the queryset. With editable PKs, `construct_instance()` or inline parent-link logic could populate the PK, bypassing this guard. The fix adds `or obj._state.adding` to catch all freshly constructed instances regardless of PK population.
  >
  > **Learnings (workflow):** The upstream 5.2 diff was directly translatable to 4.2 by substituting the 5.x `_is_pk_set()` helper call with the 4.2 idiom (`obj.pk is None`) and appending the new `obj._state.adding` condition. Running both the targeted CVE probe (`hl_cve_2026_87975`) and the touched module's full test suite (`model_formsets`) in parallel is an efficient way to confirm correctness without broader test runs.
  >
  > **Open items:** No commit or push was made per the task rules; the fix remains as a local working-tree change only. The fix covers `BaseModelFormSet`; it was not verified whether `BaseInlineFormSet` subclass overrides of `save_existing_objects` need a parallel guard in 4.2.

  The agent was told not to commit; the orchestrator committed `8e263e5` after VERIFY. Heirloom's VERIFY also ran `inline_formsets` (0 new failures), which partly covers the inline open item.

# Heirloom: hackathon log

## Project

Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched. It backports new upstream security fixes to old release lines that distributions still ship, proves which lines are actually vulnerable, adapts and verifies the fix, and asks a person only when it can't prove something. First target: Django 4.2 (EOL 2026-04-07).

## Team

- Dflame (@iamdflame)

## Stack

- Python 3.12, uv, Typer, FastAPI
- LiteLLM (model gateway), headless Claude Code (adapter)
- neatlogs (agent observability, detections)
- Entire (agent sessions as git checkpoints)
- PostGIS in Docker (GIS tests)

## Build log

content.content:
## 9. B1 findings (verified on the box 2026-10-11; these OVERRIDE earlier sections)
1. **Calibration fixes, required before L0:**
   - **C4a staging:** commit or stage the tree before `git apply -R --3way`, otherwise it fails with "does not match index".
   - **C4b fallback, the "added-condition mutant":** when the fix only adds boolean operands (e.g. `or obj._state.adding`), build the mutant by removing those operands from L's mapped symbol instead of transplanting the whole U⁻ function (a transplant drags in 5.x-only internals such as `_is_pk_set`, which gives an ERROR, i.e. MUTANT_UNBUILDABLE).
   - **C4c recursive provenance:** if blame commit C *modified* the line (a predecessor line exists in `C^`'s version of the hunk), recurse with `git blame C^` on that predecessor. Accept only when the chain ends in a **pure addition** that is not an ancestor of the merge base.
     - Concrete trap (CVE-2026-87975): the U⁻ line `if not obj._is_pk_set():` blames to `5865ff5adc` (2024, a pure rename of `if obj.pk is None:`). Non-recursive C4c would falsely "prove" 4.2 safe.
   - **Unit tests:** cover this exact case (vulnerable L + weak probe ⇒ must be UNPROVEN or AFFECTED, never NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN) and the added-condition mutant.
   - **Probe independence:** in the pipeline, the porter must never see the fix diff. The S1 probes were written after reading the fixes, so they only tested the gates.
   - **Upstream tests that ERROR on U⁻** (they reference names that only exist after the fix, as in 77050) ⇒ the porter writes a behavioural probe. For 77050, retained memory is ~4.5 MB before the fix vs <1 MB after.
2. **neatlogs reality (SDK 1.4.26):**
   - `identify(session_id, end_user_id, end_user_metadata)` has **no `parent_session_id`**. Link a CVE to its campaign with tags plus the span attribute `heirloom.campaign_id`.
   - Root spans must have kind WORKFLOW/CHAIN/AGENT/MCP_TOOL/LLM. A root GUARDRAIL span is dropped. Emit every stage **nested under an AGENT root per CVE** using `@neatlogs.span(kind=…)` / `neatlogs.trace` inside it.
   - Detection create body:
     ```
     {displayName, groupId, type:"conditional",
      runOn:{frequency: trace|span_type|span_name, span_names|span_types},
      config:{root:{type:"group", logic:AND|OR,
              children:[{type:"rule", field, operator, value}]}}}
     ```
     Operators: `= != > < >= <= contains not_contains in not_in is_empty is_not_empty`. The spec is at `https://docs.neatlogs.com/openapi/public-api.json`.
   - The `idempotency-key` must be a UUIDv4. Make it deterministic: `uuid.UUID(bytes=sha256(name)[:16], version=4)`.
   - There is no `neatlogs schema search`. Confirm the attribute field spelling with one real hit before creating all five detections. Two S4 test detections are still active; delete them after confirming.
   - The LiteLLM gateway reports `totalCostUsd: 0`, so set `heirloom.cost_usd` explicitly (from `claude -p` JSON `total_cost_usd` and token×price for LiteLLM calls).
   - Ingestion lags (~90 s+; `doctor --probe` showed TRACE_READBACK_TIMEOUT). **Mirror every detection predicate locally in the ledger** so before/after numbers never depend solely on ingestion timing. Pull the neatlogs hits/trends as corroboration.
3. **Entire:**
   - **A session started in a repo or worktree with no commits is never tracked** ("failed to get HEAD"). Always have at least one commit before starting any Claude session (interactive or `claude -p`).
   - `.entire/settings.local.json` has `{"commit_linking":"always"}` in this repo. Do the same in every pipeline worktree.

  - C1 holds;
  - every mapped symbol is absent on L (path, rename and search all fail);
  - the probe on L fails with ImportError/AttributeError naming that symbol;
  - recursive provenance (`git blame -C -C`) ends in a pure addition after merge-base 9409312eef.
  - Unit-test an add → remove → re-add history (e.g. 4971a9afe5 added a DomainNameValidator on main in 2016, yet 4.2.30 lacks one).

### 10.5 E2 campaign replay (`heirloom campaign --line 4.2 --replay`)
- **Replay** the security archive in commit order (17b93fa0, c5576670, c93a9e3c, 7d75c0b9, 3b7ae042, 904349fc), diffing advisories at each step, with LOCATE reading the archive at that ref.
- **Supersession / follow-up** (deterministic): when a new advisory's U- lines blame (trace_origin) into a fix Heirloom already backported (CVE-2026-87890 → CVE-2026-15307's 115ffd04), or a new branch label adds a follow-up commit (CVE-2026-15830 + 1eafa1a8):
  - target L = Heirloom's own earlier branch head;
  - push a fast-forward;
  - comment on and update the existing PR;
  - record a `supersedes` event.
- **One PR per CVE on the fork.** Never `clean --remote` campaign CVEs. NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN and UNPROVEN become **evidence issues on iamdflame/heirloom**, one each, with a claims table.
- **Answer poller:** `/heirloom answer <option>` comments → PolicyStore.record(kind, line) → resume. Precedents are cited by id. Never ask the same question twice.
  - Expected genuine choice: if CVE-2026-15307 is AFFECTED, "introduce Django's new DisallowedRasterLookup (a SuspiciousOperation) on 4.2, or raise plain ValueError?". Asked once; 87890's follow-up reuses the answer.
- **Budget:**
  - a per-CVE cap (HEIRLOOM_MAX_USD_PER_CVE) and a campaign cap;
  - check `GET {LITELLM_BASE}/key/info` before starting;
  - when the LiteLLM key is exhausted, the router may overflow to OPENROUTER_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY up to **$25 total overflow** (HEIRLOOM_MAX_OVERFLOW_USD=25), then stops;
  - every call's cost is recorded (the gateway reports $0, so compute it from tokens × price).

### 10.6 Read API (for a later UI; JSON only)
- `heirloom serve` (FastAPI, read-only) with /matrix, /cve/{id}, /line/{id}, /runs, /events, backed by the ledger and evals/*.json.
- `heirloom export --out site/data/` writes a static JSON snapshot. **No UI work in build sessions until the user asks.**

Write drafts to `docs/outreach/`, each built only from confirmed artifacts:
- `ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md`: Launchpad bug text for python-django (noble). Contents: facts with links, calibrated probe results, candidate patch.
- `debian-cve-2026-53878.md`: security-tracker correction proposal with the provenance proof.

"""neatlogs tracing: one WORKFLOW root per CVE run, a child span per stage.

Verified against SDK 1.4.26 on 2026-10-11 (see docs/spikes.md):
* only a WORKFLOW root finalizes; AGENT/CHAIN roots stay pending or dead-letter;
* ``identify()`` has no ``parent_session_id``: the campaign link is a tag plus
  the ``heirloom.campaign_id`` attribute;
* the gateway reports zero cost, so ``heirloom.cost_usd`` is set explicitly.

Every stage span carries all §5 attributes with explicit values (no empty
strings), and the five detection predicates are evaluated locally so the
before/after numbers never depend on ingestion timing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping
from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

Attr = str | bool | int | float

ATTR_DEFAULTS: dict[str, Attr] = {
    "cve": "NONE",
    "line": "NONE",
    "stage": "NONE",
    "verdict": "PENDING",
    "calibrated": False,
    "reach": False,

p = "heirloom/integrations/neatlogs.py"
s = open(p).read()
s = s.replace('''* the gateway reports zero cost, so ``heirloom.cost_usd`` is set explicitly.
''', '''* the gateway reports zero cost, so ``heirloom.cost_usd`` is set explicitly;
* large attributes (the ~120 KB porter prompt) are suspected of stalling
  server-side PII redaction, so (§10.2) a ``mask`` truncates every string
  attribute over 16 KB, LLM span inputs/outputs are not captured (prompts live in
  the run artifacts) and PII redaction is limited to non-LLM/AGENT span types.
''')
s = s.replace('''import os
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping''', '''import hashlib
import os
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping''')
s = s.replace('''Attr = str | bool | int | float
''', '''Attr = str | bool | int | float

MAX_ATTR_BYTES = 16 * 1024
# Span types that keep server-side PII redaction; LLM and AGENT spans are excluded.
PII_SPAN_TYPES = ["TOOL", "GUARDRAIL", "CHAIN", "WORKFLOW"]


def truncate_value(value: Any) -> Any:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    raw = value.encode()
    if len(raw) <= MAX_ATTR_BYTES:
        return value
    digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
    head = raw[:MAX_ATTR_BYTES].decode(errors="ignore")
    return f"{head}…[truncated {len(raw) - MAX_ATTR_BYTES} bytes sha256={digest}]"


def mask(span: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Truncate string attributes over 16 KB on the span and its events.

    Always returns the dict: returning None would make the SDK drop the span.
    """
    try:
        attrs = span.get("attributes")
        if isinstance(attrs, dict):
            for k, v in list(attrs.items()):
                attrs[k] = truncate_value(v)
        for event in span.get("events") or []:
            ev = event.get("attributes") if isinstance(event, dict) else None
            if isinstance(ev, dict):
                for k, v in list(ev.items()):
                    ev[k] = truncate_value(v)
    except Exception:  # a mask must never cost us the span
        pass
    return span
''')
s = s.replace('''        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.init(
            api_key=api_key, workflow_name="heirloom", instrumentations=["litellm"], tags=tags
        )''', '''        # OpenInference's default TraceConfig reads these: no prompt/response content
        # on LiteLLM (porter) spans. Full prompts are kept in the run artifacts.
        os.environ.setdefault("OPENINFERENCE_HIDE_INPUTS", "true")
        os.environ.setdefault("OPENINFERENCE_HIDE_OUTPUTS", "true")
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.init(
            api_key=api_key,
            workflow_name="heirloom",
            instrumentations=["litellm"],
            tags=tags,
            mask=mask,
            pii_span_types=PII_SPAN_TYPES,
        )''')
open(p, "w").write(s)
EOF
cat >> tests/test_detections.py <<'EOF'


def test_mask_truncates_large_strings_and_always_returns_the_dict() -> None:
    import hashlib

    from heirloom.integrations.neatlogs import MAX_ATTR_BYTES, mask

    big = "é" * MAX_ATTR_BYTES  # 2 bytes each: 32 KB
    span = {
        "attributes": {"input.value": big, "small": "ok", "n": 3, "flag": False},
        "events": [{"name": "e", "attributes": {"message": "x" * (MAX_ATTR_BYTES + 5)}}],
    }
    out = mask(span)
    assert out is span
    value = out["attributes"]["input.value"]
    assert len(value.split("…[truncated")[0].encode()) <= MAX_ATTR_BYTES
    assert f"sha256={hashlib.sha256(big.encode()).hexdigest()}" in value
    assert out["attributes"]["small"] == "ok"
    assert out["attributes"]["n"] == 3 and out["attributes"]["flag"] is False
    assert out["events"][0]["attributes"]["message"].startswith("x" * 100)
    assert "truncated 5 bytes" in out["events"][0]["attributes"]["message"]


def test_mask_survives_odd_span_shapes() -> None:
    from heirloom.integrations.neatlogs import mask

    odd: dict[str, object] = {"attributes": None, "events": [None, {"attributes": "x"}]}
    assert mask(odd) is odd
    assert mask({}) == {}
EOF

"""Eval and distro lines can never open an issue or PR, or push (BUILD-BRIEF §10.2)."""

import subprocess
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from heirloom import config, guard
from heirloom.config import LINES, LineSpec, runtime_line
from heirloom.git_ops import push
from heirloom.integrations import github
from heirloom.integrations.neatlogs import Telemetry
from heirloom.ledger import Ledger
from heirloom.pipeline import (
    adapt,
    behaviour,
    calibrate,
    decide,
    locate,
    probe,
    publish,
    run,
    verify,
)
from heirloom.pipeline.context import Ctx

TIP = "3396992e837d5146270ea8112bb622c83fa4a919"
NON_PUBLISHING = [runtime_line("eval-4.2.30", TIP, "eval"), runtime_line("ubuntu-noble", TIP, "distro")]


@pytest.fixture
def no_subprocess(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Record (and refuse) any subprocess a guarded writer might start."""
    calls: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_run(cmd: list[str], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(list(cmd))
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, "https://github.com/o/r/pull/1\n", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", fake_run)
    return calls


def writers(tmp_path: Path) -> list[Callable[[], object]]:
    body = tmp_path / "body.md"
    body.write_text("x")
    return [
        lambda: github.create_pr("iamdflame/django", "stable/4.2.x-heirloom", "b", "t", body),
        lambda: github.edit_pr_body("iamdflame/django", 1, body),
        lambda: github.close_pr("iamdflame/django", 1, "c"),
        lambda: github.create_issue("iamdflame/heirloom", "t", body),
        lambda: push(tmp_path, "fork", "HEAD:refs/heads/x"),
        lambda: push(tmp_path, "origin", "--delete", "x"),
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["eval", "distro"])
def test_non_release_lines_cannot_be_declared_publishing(kind: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="can never publish"):
        LineSpec(name="x", tip=TIP, upstream="5.2", base_branch="b", kind=kind, publish=True)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert runtime_line("x", TIP, kind).publish is False  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_runtime_lines_are_never_release_lines() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        runtime_line("x", TIP, "release")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("spec", NON_PUBLISHING, ids=lambda s: s.kind)
def test_every_writer_refuses_on_non_publishing_lines(
    spec: LineSpec, tmp_path: Path, no_subprocess: list[list[str]]
) -> None:
    with guard.publishing(spec):
        for write in writers(tmp_path):
            with pytest.raises(guard.PublishForbidden):
                write()
    assert no_subprocess == []


def test_writers_refuse_outside_any_line(tmp_path: Path, no_subprocess: list[list[str]]) -> None:
    for write in writers(tmp_path):
        with pytest.raises(guard.PublishForbidden):
            write()
    assert no_subprocess == []


def test_release_line_may_publish(tmp_path: Path, no_subprocess: list[list[str]]) -> None:
    with guard.publishing(LINES["4.2"]):
        for write in writers(tmp_path):
            write()
    assert len(no_subprocess) == 6
    assert not guard.allowed()  # the permission ends with the context


# The whole pipeline on a non-publishing line ------------------------------------

LOC = {
    "fix": "f" * 40,
    "um": "e" * 40,
    "tip": TIP,
    "base": TIP,
    "subject": "[5.2.x] Fixed CVE-X -- y",
    "message": "Fixed CVE-X",
    "upstream_test_ids": [],
    "test_files": [],
    "fix_files": [],
}
AFFECTED = {"verdict": "AFFECTED", "reason": None, "calibrated": True, "detail": "", "gates": {}}


def make_ctx(tmp_path: Path, spec: LineSpec) -> Ctx:
    s = config.load()
    s = config.Settings(**{**s.__dict__, "work": tmp_path})
    return Ctx(s, Ledger(tmp_path / "l.sqlite"), Telemetry(), spec, "CVE-X", spec.name, "r1")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("spec", NON_PUBLISHING, ids=lambda s: s.kind)
def test_pipeline_on_non_publishing_line_stops_before_publish(
    spec: LineSpec, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, no_subprocess: list[list[str]]
) -> None:
    def forbidden(*a: Any, **k: Any) -> Any:
        raise AssertionError("publish stage reached on a non-publishing line")

    monkeypatch.setattr(locate, "run", lambda ctx: LOC)
    monkeypatch.setattr(calibrate, "run_c0", lambda ctx, loc: {"structural": False})
    monkeypatch.setattr(probe, "run", lambda ctx, loc, c0, fb: {"sha": "p", "files": {}})
    monkeypatch.setattr(calibrate, "run", lambda ctx, loc, pr: {"feedback": None})
    monkeypatch.setattr(calibrate, "run_presence", lambda ctx, cal: AFFECTED)
    monkeypatch.setattr(adapt, "run", lambda *a: {"patch_sha": "x", "patch": ""})
    monkeypatch.setattr(verify, "run", lambda *a: {"ok": True})
    monkeypatch.setattr(behaviour, "run", lambda *a: {"same": True, "kind": ""})
    for name in ("commit", "push", "artifacts", "pr"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(publish, name, forbidden)
    monkeypatch.setattr(decide, "ask", forbidden)

    ctx = make_ctx(tmp_path, spec)
    with guard.publishing(spec):
        result = run.pipeline(ctx)
    assert result.status == "evaluated"
    assert result.verdict == "AFFECTED"
    assert no_subprocess == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("spec", NON_PUBLISHING, ids=lambda s: s.kind)
def test_decide_records_would_ask_instead_of_opening_an_issue(
    spec: LineSpec, tmp_path: Path, no_subprocess: list[list[str]]
) -> None:
    ctx = make_ctx(tmp_path, spec)
    unproven = {"verdict": "UNPROVEN", "reason": "ENV_SKIP", "detail": "", "gates": {}}
    with guard.publishing(spec):
        out = decide.run(ctx, unproven, None, None)
    assert out["decision"] == "would_ask"
    assert out["kind"] == "ENV_SKIP"
    assert no_subprocess == []

"""LOCATE (deterministic): the upstream fix, its trees, tests and advisory text."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from heirloom.git_ops import commit_diff, git, is_ancestor, parse_diff, rev_parse, show_file
from heirloom.integrations.neatlogs import StageSpan
from heirloom.pipeline.calibrate import symbols
from heirloom.pipeline.context import Ctx, StageFailed
from heirloom.sources.django_security import load


def upstream_test_ids(ctx: Ctx, fix: str, test_files: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Dotted ids of the test methods the fix adds, located with ast on U⁺."""
    ids: list[str] = []
    for f in parse_diff(commit_diff(ctx.repo, fix, *test_files)):
        if not f.new_path or not f.new_path.endswith(".py"):
            continue
        src = show_file(ctx.repo, fix, f.new_path) or ""
        added = {
            m[1]
            for h in f.hunks
            for line in h.added
            if (m := re.match(r"\s*def (test\w*)\(", line))
        }
        module = f.new_path.removeprefix("tests/").removesuffix(".py").replace("/", ".")
        for s in symbols(src):
            if s.qualname.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] in added and "." in s.qualname:
                ids.append(f"{module}.{s.qualname}")
    return sorted(set(ids))


def advisory_text(ctx: Ctx, fix: str, title: str) -> str:
    """The release-notes paragraph the fix adds (Django's published advisory text)."""
    notes = [
        line
        for f in parse_diff(commit_diff(ctx.repo, fix, "docs/releases/"))
        for h in f.hunks
        for line in h.added
    ]
    body = "\n".join(notes).strip()
    return f"{title}\n\n{body}" if body else title


def run(ctx: Ctx) -> dict[str, Any]:
    def body(span: StageSpan) -> dict[str, Any]:
        git(ctx.repo, "fetch", "-q", "origin", "main")
        if ctx.spec.publish and ctx.spec.base_branch:
            git(ctx.repo, "fetch", "-q", ctx.s.fork_remote, ctx.spec.base_branch)
        archive_ref = rev_parse(ctx.repo, "origin/main")
        advisories = load(ctx.repo, archive_ref)
        if ctx.cve not in advisories:
            raise StageFailed(f"{ctx.cve} is not in security.txt at {archive_ref[:10]}")
        adv = advisories[ctx.cve]
        fix = rev_parse(ctx.repo, adv.fix_commit(ctx.spec.upstream))
        message = git(ctx.repo, "log", "-1", "--format=%B", fix)
        if ctx.cve not in message or not (
            f"Fixed {ctx.cve}" in message or "Backport of" in message
        ):
            raise StageFailed(f"{fix[:10]} message does not say 'Fixed {ctx.cve}'/'Backport of'")
        files = git(ctx.repo, "diff", "--name-only", f"{fix}^", fix).split()
        fix_files = [f for f in files if f.startswith("django/")]
        test_files = [f for f in files if f.startswith("tests/")]
        if not fix_files:
            raise StageFailed(f"{fix[:10]} changes no django/ files")
        um = rev_parse(ctx.repo, f"{fix}^")
        tip = rev_parse(ctx.repo, ctx.spec.tip)
        if ctx.spec.publish and ctx.spec.base_branch:
            base = rev_parse(ctx.repo, f"{ctx.s.fork_remote}/{ctx.spec.base_branch}")
            if not is_ancestor(ctx.repo, tip, base):
                raise StageFailed(
                    f"{ctx.spec.base_branch} does not contain the line tip {tip[:10]}"
                )
        else:
            base = tip  # non-publishing lines work on the tip itself, never the fork
        merge_base = git(ctx.repo, "merge-base", um, tip).strip()
        subject = message.splitlines()[0]
        span.set("claim_id", f"{ctx.cve}/{ctx.line}/locate")
        span.set("fix_sha", fix)
        return {
            "cve": ctx.cve,
            "title": adv.title,
            "date": adv.date.isoformat(),
            "url": adv.url or "",
            "archive_ref": archive_ref,
            "fix": fix,
            "um": um,
            "tip": tip,
            "base": base,
            "merge_base": merge_base,
            "subject": subject,
            "message": message,
            "fix_files": fix_files,
            "test_files": test_files,
            "upstream_test_ids": upstream_test_ids(ctx, fix, test_files),
            "advisory": advisory_text(ctx, fix, adv.title),
        }

    return ctx.stage("locate", {"cve": ctx.cve, "line": ctx.line, "tip": ctx.spec.tip}, body)

### 10.4 Distro lines (Thread B, own `git clone --shared` + own HEIRLOOM_WORK)
- **Builder** (`heirloom/lines/distro.py`):
  1. Download the orig and debian tarballs into fresh empty directories.
  2. `git worktree add -B distro/ubuntu-noble 4.2.11`.
  3. Assert that `diff -r` between the tarball's django/ and the worktree's django/ is empty (otherwise commit an "orig delta").
  4. Apply `debian/patches/series` in order with `patch -p1`, ONE COMMIT PER PATCH: message = the DEP-3 header, trailer `Distro-Patch: <file>`.
  5. Record the tarball sha256s and the tip sha.
  - Same for **debian-trixie on tag 4.2.28** (its six non-CVE patches).
- **Mutant `distro_revert`:** the line minus one distro patch (revert that commit). Use it as C4a on distro lines.
- **Matrix** (`heirloom matrix --lines 4.2.30,debian-trixie,ubuntu-noble`): reuse each CVE's calibrated probe via on_line() → `evals/matrix.json`.
  - **Cross-validation expectation:** the 5 CVEs Ubuntu fixed should be NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN on noble; report honestly where they are not.
  - Also run the Mar/Apr 2026 backtest probes on debian-trixie (4.2.28 lacks the official 4.2.29/4.2.30 fixes).
- **CVE-2026-87890 probe** (deterministic; no GDAL I/O, no network):
  - a SimpleTestCase, no spatial models;
  - `Recorder` subclasses the tree's `django.contrib.gis.gdal.GDALRaster`; its `__init__` appends `type(ds_input)` to a list, then raises `GDALException`;
  - under `mock.patch("django.contrib.gis.gdal.GDALRaster", Recorder)`, call `PointField(srid=4326).get_prep_value(b"...")` and `RasterField().get_prep_value(b"...")`, each in try/except Exception: pass;
  - assert the recorded list is empty;
  - **test bytes only** (str/dict belong to CVE-2026-15307).
  - Calibration: FAIL on U-=dd0558d1^, PASS on U+=dd0558d1. Then run it on 4.2.30 and on ubuntu-noble.
  - Give the porter a general hint for GIS/native-library CVEs: "no spatial models; call Field.get_prep_value; intercept public constructors with unittest.mock".
- **CVE-2026-53878 "absent symbol" path** → NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN only when all of these hold:
  - C1 holds;
  - every mapped symbol is absent on L (path, rename and search all fail);

def lfix(ctx: Ctx, base: str, probe: dict[str, str], patch: str | None) -> Path:
    """Reset ``Lfix`` to ``base`` + probe (+ patch). Never call after publish.commit."""
    path = ctx.tree_path("Lfix")
    if not path.exists():
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        git(ctx.repo, "worktree", "prune")
        git(ctx.repo, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-B", ctx.branch, str(path), base)
    else:
        git(path, "checkout", "-q", "-f", "-B", ctx.branch, base)
        git(path, "reset", "-q", "--hard", base)
        git(path, "clean", "-q", "-fdx", "-e", ".claude/", "-e", ".entire/")
    ctx.install_probe(path, probe)
    if patch:
        git(path, "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", "-", input=patch)
    entire.enable(path, ctx.s.fork)
    return path

"""E1 backtest (BUILD-BRIEF §6, §10.3): ground truth = the Django fellows' real 4.2 patches.

Cases (set ``django-4.2-2026``):
* positive: each Feb/Mar/Apr 2026 CVE the fellows fixed on 4.2. L = their 4.2 fix
  commit's parent. Truth AFFECTED, and their own 4.2 regression test must pass on
  L + our patch.
* negative (fixed twin): L = the fellows' 4.2 fix commit. Truth: not affected. It
  reuses the positive's calibrated probe, so no fixed source reaches the porter.
* extra: CVE-2025-27556, fixed upstream only on 5.1/5.0 (via upstream_fallbacks) and
  shipped without a 4.2 patch while 4.2 was supported; L = tag 4.2.20.

Pipelines: ``v2`` is the full Heirloom pipeline on a non-publishing eval line; ``v1``
is the naive baseline (cherry-pick the upstream fix, let the model resolve conflicts,
trust its own run of the upstream tests, no calibration). Results → evals/results.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from heirloom.config import Settings, runtime_line
from heirloom.git_ops import commit_diff, ensure_worktree, git, parse_diff, rev_parse, show_file
from heirloom.ledger import Ledger
from heirloom.models.router import Budget, Router
from heirloom.pipeline.calibrate import symbols
from heirloom.pipeline.run import calibrated_probe, execute
from heirloom.sources.django_security import load
from heirloom.verify.runner import Runner

SET = "django-4.2-2026"
POSITIVE_DATES = (date(2026, 2, 3), date(2026, 3, 3), date(2026, 4, 7))
EXTRA = {"CVE-2025-27556": "4.2.20"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Case:
    cve: str
    kind: str  # positive | negative | extra
    tip: str  # L
    truth: str  # AFFECTED | NOT_AFFECTED
    fellows_fix: str | None  # the fellows' 4.2 commit (positives/negatives)

    @property
    def line(self) -> str:
        return f"bt-{self.kind[:3]}-{self.tip[:10]}"


def cases(repo: Path) -> list[Case]:
    advisories = load(repo)
    out: list[Case] = []
    for adv in sorted(advisories.values(), key=lambda a: (a.date, a.cve)):
        if adv.date not in POSITIVE_DATES or "4.2" not in adv.commits:
            continue
        fellows = rev_parse(repo, adv.commits["4.2"][0])
        out.append(Case(adv.cve, "positive", rev_parse(repo, f"{fellows}^"), "AFFECTED", fellows))
        out.append(Case(adv.cve, "negative", fellows, "NOT_AFFECTED", fellows))
    for cve, tag in EXTRA.items():
        out.append(Case(cve, "extra", rev_parse(repo, tag), "NOT_AFFECTED", None))
    return out


def fellows_test_ids(repo: Path, fellows: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    """(test files, dotted test ids) the fellows' 4.2 commit adds."""
    files = [
        f
        for f in git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", f"{fellows}^", fellows).split()
        if f.startswith("tests/")
    ]
    ids: list[str] = []
    for d in parse_diff(commit_diff(repo, fellows, *files)):
        if not d.new_path or not d.new_path.endswith(".py"):
            continue
        added = {
            m[1]
            for h in d.hunks
            for line in h.added
            if (m := re.match(r"\s*def (test\w*)\(", line))
        }
        module = d.new_path.removeprefix("tests/").removesuffix(".py").replace("/", ".")
        src = show_file(repo, fellows, d.new_path) or ""
        ids += [
            f"{module}.{s.qualname}"
            for s in symbols(src)
            if "." in s.qualname and s.qualname.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] in added
        ]
    return files, sorted(set(ids))


def fellows_test_passes(
    s: Settings, case: Case, patch: str, work: Path
) -> tuple[bool | None, str]:
    """Run the fellows' own 4.2 regression tests on L + ``patch``."""
    assert case.fellows_fix is not None
    files, ids = fellows_test_ids(s.django_repo, case.fellows_fix)
    if not ids:
        return None, "fellows' commit adds no test methods"
    tree = ensure_worktree(s.django_repo, work / "fellows-check", case.tip)
    for text, what in ((patch, "our patch"), (commit_diff(s.django_repo, case.fellows_fix, *files, context=3), "fellows' tests")):
        if not text.strip():
            continue
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(tree), "apply", "--3way", "-"], input=text, capture_output=True, text=True
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return False, f"{what} does not apply: {proc.stderr.strip()[:200]}"
    r = Runner(python=s.test_python, timeout=s.test_timeout).run(
        tree, ids, log_path=work / "fellows-check.log"
    )
    return r.outcome == "PASS", f"{r.outcome} {r.summary} ({len(ids)} tests)"


def _latest_output(ledger: Ledger, cve: str, line: str, stage: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    rows = [r for r in ledger.stages(cve, line) if r.key.stage == stage and r.status == "done"]
    return max(rows, key=lambda r: r.key.attempt).output if rows else None


def run_v2(s: Settings, case: Case) -> dict[str, Any]:
    spec = runtime_line(case.line, case.tip, "eval")
    reuse: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    if case.kind == "negative":
        ledger = Ledger(s.ledger_path)
        reuse = calibrated_probe(ledger, case.cve, Case(case.cve, "positive", "", "", None).line)
        positive_line = next(
            (c.line for c in cases(s.django_repo) if c.cve == case.cve and c.kind == "positive"),
            None,
        )
        reuse = calibrated_probe(ledger, case.cve, positive_line) if positive_line else None
        ledger.close()
        if reuse is None:
            return {"verdict": "SKIPPED", "reason": "positive has no calibrated probe to reuse"}
    start = time.monotonic()
    result = execute(s, case.cve, spec, reuse_probe=reuse)
    minutes = (time.monotonic() - start) / 60
    ledger = Ledger(s.ledger_path)
    rows = ledger.stages(case.cve, case.line)
    decide = _latest_output(ledger, case.cve, case.line, "decide") or {}
    adapt = _latest_output(ledger, case.cve, case.line, "adapt")
    cost_unknown = any(
        r.key.stage == "adapt" and r.status == "failed" and "interrupted" in (r.error or "")
        for r in rows
    )
    ledger.close()
    out: dict[str, Any] = {
        "verdict": result.verdict,
        "reason": result.reason,
        "status": result.status,
        "run_id": result.run_id,
        "escalated": result.reason != "NONE" and result.verdict == "UNPROVEN"
        or "would_ask" in str(decide.get("decision", "")),
        "decision": decide.get("decision"),
        "reused_probe": reuse is not None,
        "cost_usd": round(result.cost_usd, 4),
        "cost_unknown": cost_unknown,
        "minutes": round(minutes, 2),
        "message": result.message,
    }
    if case.kind == "positive" and result.verdict == "AFFECTED" and adapt:
        ok, detail = fellows_test_passes(s, case, adapt["patch"], s.cve_dir(case.cve, case.line))
        out["fellows_test_passes"], out["fellows_test_detail"] = ok, detail
    return out


# v1: naive baseline ---------------------------------------------------------------

V1_PROMPT = """Resolve the git merge conflict in this file from cherry-picking an upstream \
Django security fix onto an older release. Keep the older release's code and apply the \
fix's intent. Reply with ONLY the complete resolved file in one ```python fenced block.

File: {path}
```
{text}
```"""


def run_v1(s: Settings, case: Case, budget_usd: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Cherry-pick the upstream fix; the model resolves conflicts; trust upstream tests."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    work = s.cve_dir(case.cve, f"v1-{case.line}")
    tree = ensure_worktree(s.django_repo, work / "tree", case.tip)
    adv = load(s.django_repo)[case.cve]
    series = adv.first_series(("5.2", "5.1", "5.0"))
    fixes = adv.fix_commits(series)
    spent = 0.0
    router = Router(s, Budget(budget_usd, lambda: spent))
    conflicts: list[str] = []
    for sha in fixes:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(tree), "cherry-pick", "-n", "-X", "patience", sha],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )
        if proc.returncode == 0:
            continue
        for path in git(tree, "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U").split():
            conflicts.append(path)
            if not path.endswith(".py"):
                git(tree, "checkout", "--ours", "--", path)
                continue
            text = (tree / path).read_text()
            res = router.complete(
                s.adapt_model,
                [{"role": "user", "content": V1_PROMPT.format(path=path, text=text[:150_000])}],
                max_tokens=16000,
            )
            spent += res.cost_usd
            m = re.search(r"```(?:python)?\n(.*?)```", res.text, re.S)
            if m:
                (tree / path).write_text(m[1])
            git(tree, "add", "--", path)
    patch = git(tree, "diff", "HEAD", "--", "django/")
    files = [f for f in git(tree, "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD").split() if f.startswith("tests/")]
    up_ids: list[str] = []
    for d in parse_diff(git(tree, "diff", "-U0", "HEAD", "--", *files)) if files else []:
        added = {m[1] for h in d.hunks for line in h.added if (m := re.match(r"\s*def (test\w*)\(", line))}
        module = (d.new_path or "").removeprefix("tests/").removesuffix(".py").replace("/", ".")
        src = (tree / (d.new_path or "")).read_text() if d.new_path else ""
        up_ids += [f"{module}.{x.qualname}" for x in symbols(src) if "." in x.qualname and x.qualname.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] in added]
    own = None
    if up_ids:
        r = Runner(python=s.test_python, timeout=s.test_timeout).run(
            tree, sorted(set(up_ids)), log_path=work / "v1-upstream-tests.log"
        )
        own = r.outcome
    verdict = "AFFECTED" if patch.strip() else "NOT_AFFECTED"
    out: dict[str, Any] = {
        "verdict": verdict,
        "reason": "NONE",
        "own_upstream_tests": own,
        "conflicts": conflicts,
        "escalated": False,
        "cost_usd": round(spent, 4),
        "cost_unknown": False,
        "minutes": round((time.monotonic() - start) / 60, 2),
    }
    if case.kind == "positive" and patch.strip():
        ok, detail = fellows_test_passes(s, case, patch, work)
        out["fellows_test_passes"], out["fellows_test_detail"] = ok, detail
    return out


# Results ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def correct(case: Case, verdict: str) -> bool | None:
    if verdict == "UNPROVEN" or verdict == "SKIPPED":
        return None
    if case.truth == "AFFECTED":
        return verdict == "AFFECTED"
    return verdict == "NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN" or verdict == "NOT_AFFECTED"


def summarize(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    decided = [r for r in rows if r["correct"] is not None]
    pos = [r for r in rows if r["kind"] == "positive"]
    known_cost = [r["cost_usd"] for r in rows if not r.get("cost_unknown")]
    return {
        "cases": len(rows),
        "decided": len(decided),
        "verdict_accuracy": round(sum(r["correct"] for r in decided) / len(decided), 3) if decided else None,
        "false_not_affected": sum(
            1 for r in rows if r["truth"] == "AFFECTED" and r["verdict"] in ("NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN", "NOT_AFFECTED")
        ),
        "false_affected": sum(1 for r in rows if r["truth"] == "NOT_AFFECTED" and r["verdict"] == "AFFECTED"),
        "unproven": sum(1 for r in rows if r["verdict"] == "UNPROVEN"),
        "escalation_rate": round(sum(bool(r.get("escalated")) for r in rows) / len(rows), 3) if rows else None,
        "fellows_test_pass": f"{sum(1 for r in pos if r.get('fellows_test_passes'))}/{len(pos)}",
        "usd_per_case": round(sum(known_cost) / len(known_cost), 4) if known_cost else None,
        "usd_total": round(sum(known_cost), 4),
        "cost_unknown_cases": sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("cost_unknown")),
        "minutes_per_case": round(sum(r["minutes"] for r in rows if "minutes" in r) / len(rows), 2) if rows else None,
    }


def record(path: Path, pipeline: str, case: Case, result: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {"set": SET, "runs": {}}
    row = {**asdict(case), "line": case.line, "pipeline": pipeline, **result}
    row["correct"] = correct(case, result["verdict"])
    row["at"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
    runs = data.setdefault("runs", {}).setdefault(pipeline, {})
    runs[f"{case.cve}:{case.kind}"] = row
    data["summary"] = {p: summarize(list(r.values())) for p, r in data["runs"].items()}
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, default=str) + "\n")
    return row

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RESULTS = ROOT / "evals" / "results.json"
README = ROOT / "README.md"
START, END = "<!-- e1:start -->", "<!-- e1:end -->"
LABELS = {
    "v2": "v2 · Heirloom (calibrated)",
    "v1": "v1 · naive (cherry-pick + LLM, no calibration)",
}


def pct(x: float | None) -> str:
    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{100 * x:.0f}%"


def table(data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    rows = [
        "| Pipeline | Cases | Verdict accuracy (decided) | False NOT_AFFECTED | "
        "False AFFECTED | UNPROVEN | Fellows' 4.2 test passes | Escalation rate | "
        "$ / case | Min / case |",
        "|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    for name in ("v2", "v1"):
        s = data.get("summary", {}).get(name)
        if not s:
            continue
        usd = "n/a" if s["usd_per_case"] is None else f"${s['usd_per_case']:.2f}"
        unknown = f" (+{s['cost_unknown_cases']} unknown)" if s["cost_unknown_cases"] else ""
        rows.append(
            f"| {LABELS[name]} | {s['cases']} | {pct(s['verdict_accuracy'])} "
            f"({s['decided']} decided) | **{s['false_not_affected']}** | "
            f"{s['false_affected']} | {s['unproven']} | {s['fellows_test_pass']} | "
            f"{pct(s['escalation_rate'])} | {usd}{unknown} | {s['minutes_per_case']} |"
        )
    per_case = [
        "",
        "<details><summary>Per case</summary>",
        "",
        "| CVE | Case | Truth | v2 verdict | v2 fellows' test | v1 verdict | v1 fellows' test |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    runs = data.get("runs", {})
    keys = sorted(set(runs.get("v2", {})) | set(runs.get("v1", {})))
    for k in keys:
        a, b = runs.get("v2", {}).get(k, {}), runs.get("v1", {}).get(k, {})
        base = a or b
        per_case.append(
            f"| {base['cve']} | {base['kind']} | {base['truth']} | "
            f"{a.get('verdict', '—')} {('(' + a['reason'] + ')') if a.get('reason') not in (None, 'NONE') else ''} | "
            f"{a.get('fellows_test_passes', '—')} | {b.get('verdict', '—')} | "
            f"{b.get('fellows_test_passes', '—')} |"
        )
    per_case += ["", "</details>"]
    note = (
        f"\n_Set `{data.get('set')}`; rendered from [`evals/results.json`](evals/results.json) "
        "by `evals/render_readme.py`. Accuracy counts only decided cases; UNPROVEN means "
        "Heirloom declined to claim either way and would ask a human._"
    )
    return "\n".join(rows) + note + "\n" + "\n".join(per_case)


def main() -> int:
    data = json.loads(RESULTS.read_text())
    text = README.read_text()
    block = f"{START}\n{table(data)}\n{END}"
    if START in text and END in text:
        head, rest = text.split(START, 1)
        _, tail = rest.split(END, 1)
        text = head + block + tail
    else:
        text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## E1 backtest: Django 4.2, 2026 CVEs\n\n" + block + "\n"
    README.write_text(text)
    print(f"rendered {README}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

entries.name: TaskStop
entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

from django.test import SimpleTestCase
from django.utils.http import url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme


# The fix for CVE-2025-27556 adds a MAX_URL_LENGTH cap (2048 characters) to
# url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme() to prevent DoS via NFKC normalization of
# very long Unicode strings on Windows.
#
# Vulnerable behaviour: no length limit, so an arbitrarily long URL that
# looks structurally valid is accepted (returns True).
# Fixed behaviour: URLs longer than MAX_URL_LENGTH are rejected (returns False).

MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048  # value introduced by the fix


class CVE202527556UrlLengthLimitTest(SimpleTestCase):
    """
    url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme() must reject URLs that exceed
    MAX_URL_LENGTH to avoid the NFKC-normalization DoS on Windows.
    """

    allowed_host = "example.com"

    def _make_url(self, extra_chars):
        """Return a URL whose host matches allowed_host with extra path chars."""
        return "http://{}/{}".format(self.allowed_host, extra_chars)

    def test_url_at_max_length_is_accepted(self):
        """A URL at exactly MAX_URL_LENGTH should still be evaluated normally."""
        # Build a URL that is exactly MAX_URL_LENGTH characters using safe ASCII.
        prefix = "http://{}/".format(self.allowed_host)
        padding = "a" * (MAX_URL_LENGTH - len(prefix))
        url = prefix + padding
        self.assertEqual(len(url), MAX_URL_LENGTH)
        result = url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(
            url, allowed_hosts={self.allowed_host}
        )
        # A well-formed URL at the boundary should be accepted.
        self.assertTrue(result)

    def test_url_exceeding_max_length_is_rejected(self):
        """
        A URL longer than MAX_URL_LENGTH must be rejected (return False).

        On vulnerable Django 4.2 code there is no length guard, so a
        structurally valid URL with a matching host returns True regardless
        of length — this assertion will FAIL on the vulnerable tree.
        """
        # Use multi-byte Unicode characters (like the upstream regression test)
        # to create a URL well beyond MAX_URL_LENGTH.
        extra = "\u00e9" * (MAX_URL_LENGTH + 500)  # 'é' repeated
        url = "http://{}/{}".format(self.allowed_host, extra)
        self.assertGreater(len(url), MAX_URL_LENGTH)
        result = url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(
            url, allowed_hosts={self.allowed_host}
        )
        # Fixed code must return False for over-length URLs.
        self.assertFalse(result)

import re

from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from heirloom.pipeline.presence import Gate

LOOKUP_ERROR = re.compile(r"\b(ImportError|ModuleNotFoundError|AttributeError)\b")


def definitions(source: str) -> set[str]:
    """Names a module defines at any depth: classes, functions, assignment targets."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(source)
    except SyntaxError:
        return set()
    out: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef | ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
            out.add(node.name)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign | ast.AnnAssign):
            targets = node.targets if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else [node.target]
            for t in targets:
                for n in ast.walk(t):
                    if isinstance(n, ast.Name):
                        out.add(n.id)
    return out


def defined_on(repo: Path, ref: str, name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Python files under django/ on ``ref`` that define ``name``."""
    hits = git(repo, "grep", "-l", "-w", "-F", "-e", name, ref, "--", "django/", check=False)
    found: list[str] = []
    for hit in hits.splitlines():
        path = hit.split(":", 1)[1]
        if path.endswith(".py") and name in definitions(show_file(repo, ref, path) or ""):
            found.append(path)
    return found


def missing_name(repo: Path, ref: str, qualname: str) -> str | None:
    """The outermost component of ``qualname`` that nothing in L's django/ defines."""
    for part in qualname.split("."):
        if not defined_on(repo, ref, part):
            return part
    return None

with an ImportError, which the verdict table treats as PROBE_ERROR. This gate lets
PRESENCE prove NOT_AFFECTED only when *all* of the following hold (C1 is checked
by the verdict table itself):

1. every mapped fix symbol is absent on L: same path, rename tracking and the repo
   search all fail, and no ``class``/``def``/assignment anywhere in L's django/
   defines the missing name;
2. the probe ERRORs on every L run, and every error is an ImportError /
   ModuleNotFoundError / AttributeError that names a missing symbol;
3. recursive provenance with ``git blame -C -C`` (copies from other files count)
   of every line the fix deletes or changes inside the symbol (the C4c lines;
   the symbol's ``class``/``def`` line when the fix only inserts) ends in a pure
   addition that descends from the merge base and is not one of its ancestors,
   and no L commit says "Backport of" that addition.

Ancestry, never dates: 4971a9afe5 ("Added a DomainNameValidator") has a 2016
author date but was committed in 2024, after the 4.2 branch point.

Why not always trace the ``class`` line: in 4971a9afe5 git's diff aligns
``class DomainNameValidator(RegexValidator):`` with the removed (actually moved)
``class URLValidator(RegexValidator):`` header, so recursive blame of the header
follows URLValidator back to 2015. The fix's changed lines are what carries the
vulnerability, and they all end in 4971a9afe5's pure addition.

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import re
from collections import Counter
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from heirloom.git_ops import FileDiff, git, is_ancestor, show_file
from heirloom.pipeline.presence import Gate

LOOKUP_ERROR = re.compile(r"\b(ImportError|ModuleNotFoundError|AttributeError)\b")


def definitions(source: str) -> set[str]:
    """Names a module defines at any depth: classes, functions, assignment targets."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(source)
    except SyntaxError:
        return set()
    out: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef | ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
            out.add(node.name)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign | ast.AnnAssign):
            targets = node.targets if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else [node.target]
            for t in targets:
                for n in ast.walk(t):
                    if isinstance(n, ast.Name):
                        out.add(n.id)
    return out


def defined_on(repo: Path, ref: str, name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Python files under django/ on ``ref`` that define ``name``."""
    hits = git(repo, "grep", "-l", "-w", "-F", "-e", name, ref, "--", "django/", check=False)
    found: list[str] = []
    for hit in hits.splitlines():
        path = hit.split(":", 1)[1]
        if path.endswith(".py") and name in definitions(show_file(repo, ref, path) or ""):
            found.append(path)
    return found


def missing_name(repo: Path, ref: str, qualname: str) -> str | None:
    """The outermost component of ``qualname`` that nothing in L's django/ defines."""
    for part in qualname.split("."):
        if not defined_on(repo, ref, part):
            return part
    return None

### 2026-10-11 (session B3) · Day-2 foundation, E1 backtest, distro lines

This session was tracked by Entire from the start: `entire session current` showed session `f5117257-5211-42ae-823c-32aa228a28d9` active. Two threads ran: A (this conversation) and B (a subagent in its own worktree, Django clone and work dir, merged as `28504fe`). 37 commits on `main` since `042d547`.

**Spikes**
- **LiteLLM budget** ([evals/litellm_budget.json](evals/litellm_budget.json), from `GET /key/info`):
  - At the start: $2.96 spent of $20 (30-day window, resets 2026-11-01).
  - At the end (15:22 UTC): **$20.35 of $20, so the key is exhausted.** After that the router overflowed to the OpenRouter key under the new policy: 26 calls between 14:40 and 15:22, $3.76 of the $25 cap (all v1 conflict resolutions).
  - Heirloom's own cost records (token × list price, plus `claude -p`'s `total_cost_usd`) come to roughly half of what the gateway billed today. See open problems.
- **neatlogs** ([evals/neatlogs_ingestion.json](evals/neatlogs_ingestion.json)):
  - With the §10.2 settings (16 KB attribute mask that always returns the dict, LLM input/output capture off, `pii_span_types` = TOOL/GUARDRAIL/CHAIN/WORKFLOW, WORKFLOW root, flush + shutdown), the eval-line run of CVE-2026-87975 (`heirloom cve … --line eval-4.2.30 --kind eval`) was stored: trace `b6559615…`, **finalized, 12 spans**, including the LLM span. The 12- to 21-span backtest traces that followed finalized too.
  - Detections do evaluate on this project: a control detection `status = OK` on `presence` spans got 23 hits.
  - **Ten spellings of a custom attribute** (`heirloom.stage`, `attributes.heirloom.stage`, `span.attributes.…`, `metadata.…`, `heirloom_stage`, `attributes["heirloom.stage"]`, `span_attributes.…`, `custom_attributes.…`, `attributes.heirloom_stage`, plus `name`) **got 0 hits**. So the five §5 detections were *not* created, and the two S4 test detections were *not* deleted (both conditional on a confirmed spelling). The probe detections were deleted again; deletion needs `{"confirmation": <id>}`.
  - The earlier unmasked 100 KB experiment trace also finalized eventually, so the old dead-lettering was at least partly transient on neatlogs' side.

**Foundation (§10.2), Thread A**
- **`LineSpec`:** gains `kind` (release/eval/distro), `publish` and `upstream_fallbacks`. Runtime lines come from `heirloom cve CVE --line NAME --tip REF --kind eval|distro`, and the spec is stored with the run for `resume`.
- **Deny-by-default publish guard** (`heirloom/guard.py`): it runs inside every GitHub write and every `git push`. `tests/test_publish_guard.py` (12 tests) proves eval and distro lines can never open an issue or PR, or push, at the spec level, at every writer, and through a full `pipeline()` run.
- **Multi-commit fixes:** the parser keeps every fix commit per series, including the "5.2.18" follow-up of CVE-2026-15830. LOCATE uses upstream fallbacks (CVE-2025-27556 → 5.1).
- **Calibration split:** `reference()` covers U⁻/U⁺ and is shared across lines; `on_line(tip)` covers C2–C4. Reach ignores docstring- and comment-only hunks. Reuse mode needs a C1-discriminating probe and never retries.
- **Fixes found by the backtest:**
  - Python 3.12 `[msg]` subtest headers had been classified as ERROR.
  - Message-literal BEHAVIOUR check.
  - The adapter must keep upstream messages.
  - Leakage guard narrowed (new whole lines only; not the L-source sections).
  - Probe imports widened to the stdlib minus time/network/process.
  - Changed (not only added) test methods count as test ids.
  - GIS fixes run on PostGIS (`heirloom/verify/django_settings/test_postgis.py`).
  - Empty coverage means zero reach.
  - Overflow only after the key is exhausted, with a global cap.
  - Transient gateway 5xx/429 retried.
- **Eval leakage guard:** ADAPT on eval/distro lines runs in a one-commit repo (`git init` + depth-1 fetch of L) with `git log`/`git show` disallowed. A test proves the fellows' fix is unreachable from it.

**E1 backtest** ([evals/results.json](evals/results.json), table in README via `evals/render_readme.py`)

| | v2 (Heirloom) | v1 (naive) |
|---|---|---|
| Cases | 27 (16 decided) | 27 (27 decided) |
| **False NOT_AFFECTED** | **0** | **1** (CVE-2026-1285: v1's own upstream tests FAILED, yet the empty patch counted as "not affected") |
| False AFFECTED | 1 (CVE-2025-27556) | 3 (CVE-2025-27556, 25673 and 33034 twins) |
| Accuracy on decided | 93.8% | 85.2% |
| UNPROVEN / escalation rate | 9 / 37% | 0 / 0% |
| Fellows' own 4.2 test passes on our patch | 7/13 | 11/13 |
| $ total (estimate) / min per case | $3.59 / 1.0 | $3.99 / 1.96 |

- **Spike:** v2 ran first on CVE-2026-1287 and CVE-2026-25674, then from a clean state after fixing what it found. False NOT_AFFECTED stayed 0 throughout, so there was no stop.
- **v2 UNPROVEN positives:** 1207 (NON_DISCRIMINATING), 1285, 25674 and 3902 (NO_REACH: the probe missed one of the fix's call sites), 25673 (PROBE_ERROR). The 1207 and 25673 twins were skipped (no C1 probe to reuse).
- **CVE-2026-1287 (v2 AFFECTED, fellows' test fails):** a genuine choice. Upstream changed the alias error message. 4.2's existing tests assert the old message, so adopting the new one broke them and the adapter may not edit tests. VERIFY forced the old message back, BEHAVIOUR flagged the difference, and DECIDE recorded `would_ask`. The fellows solved it by editing their tests.
- **CVE-2025-27556 (both pipelines AFFECTED; truth not affected):**
  - Django's 2025-04-02 advisory lists only main, 5.2 (RC), 5.1 and 5.0.
  - 4.2.20's vendored `_urlsplit` never runs the NFKC netloc check.
  - The probe asserted the fix's *mitigation* (a URL length cap) rather than the slow mechanism, and C1–C3 all held. This is a known gap: calibration cannot yet tell a mitigation probe from a mechanism probe.
- **v1's higher fellows'-test rate is real.** Cherry-picking the upstream fix wholesale (tests included) matches the fellows' 4.2 commits closely, while v2 declines to patch what it cannot prove.

**Distro lines, Thread B** ([evals/distro_lines.json](evals/distro_lines.json), [evals/matrix.json](evals/matrix.json), [evals/cve_2026_87890.json](evals/cve_2026_87890.json), [evals/cve_2026_53878.json](evals/cve_2026_53878.json), [evals/new_probes.json](evals/new_probes.json))
- **Lines built, one commit per patch** (DEP-3 header + `Distro-Patch:` trailer; `diff -r` of django/ against the orig tarball empty; sha256s recorded):
  - ubuntu-noble 3:4.2.11-1ubuntu1.18: 48 patches, tip `f566e91a2c`.
  - debian-trixie 3:4.2.28-0+deb13u2: 6 patches, tip `5c81215443`.
- **CVE-2026-87890:** the hand-written bytes-recorder probe (labelled as such, not from the porter) FAILs ×3 on dd0558d1^ and PASSes ×3 on dd0558d1. It is **AFFECTED on 4.2.30 and on ubuntu-noble**: noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path open.
- **CVE-2026-53878:** **NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN on 4.2.30** via the absent-symbol path:
  - C1 holds.
  - L ERRORs ×3 with an `ImportError` naming `DomainNameValidator`.
  - `blame -C -C` provenance of the 14 changed lines ends at 4971a9afe5, a pure addition committed *after* the merge base. Its 2016 author date is misleading; the brief's "re-add" premise is wrong and is covered by a synthetic test instead.
- **Matrix** (33 CVEs, reused probes, $0 model spend):
  - 4.2.30: 7 AFFECTED, 7 NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN, 6 UNPROVEN, 13 without a probe.
  - debian-trixie: 11 / 4 / 5 / 13.
  - ubuntu-noble: 3 / 11 / 6 / 13.
  - Cross-check against Ubuntu's own patches: 10 of the 15 CVEs Ubuntu patched are NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN on noble, 5 UNPROVEN, **0 AFFECTED**. Of the 5 post-EOL CVEs Ubuntu fixed, 4 are NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN; 15307 is UNPROVEN (NO_REACH, the probe design overrides a fix symbol).
- **Thread B spent $0.81** of its $3 cap (LiteLLM only).

**Tests that actually ran**
- pytest at `HEAD` after the merge: **162 passed**: test_absent 12, test_backtest 7, test_calibrate 11, test_claims 5, test_decide 4, test_detections 6, test_distro 17, test_django_security 9, test_handwritten 4, test_ledger 12, test_matrix 5, test_overflow 5, test_presence 13, test_probe_rules 16, test_publish_guard 12, test_runner 23, test_runner_import_error 1.
- ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy --strict: clean (58 files).
- Runs:
  - the eval line for CVE-2026-87975 (twice: once fresh, once re-calibrating);
  - E1 v2, 27 cases; E1 v1, 27 cases;
